intro: If you've got a blocked drain in Borthwickroad, you'll want it sorted quickly — a slow-draining sink can become a backed-up nightmare within hours, and an outdoor drain blockage in a small, tightly-knit community like this one isn't something you want sitting around. That range covers the vast majority of jobs, from a straightforward kitchen sink unblock through to a more stubborn external drain that needs high-pressure jetting. Emergency call-outs, which are common given how quickly drains can deteriorate, may carry an additional out-of-hours charge.
localContext: Borthwickroad sits in Midlothian and has a mix of property types that each bring their own drainage quirks. The older stone-built properties and period cottages in the area often have original clay or cast iron drainage runs that have been in the ground for decades — sometimes well over a century. These older pipes are far more prone to root ingress from nearby trees and shrubs, joint displacement as the ground shifts, and gradual scale build-up over the years. Modern estates in Borthwickroad tend to use plastic pipework which is more resilient, but still susceptible to blockages from fat, wipes, and sediment. Being in a moderately hard water area also plays a role — limescale accumulates inside pipes and around waste fittings over time, narrowing the bore and making blockages more likely and more stubborn to shift. It's worth factoring this in if you've had repeat blockages in the same area of the house.
serviceDetail: When a drainage engineer arrives at your Borthwickroad property, the first thing they'll do is assess where the blockage is and what's likely causing it. This usually involves a quick inspection of the visible access points — inspection chambers, gully covers, and any accessible rodding eyes — to pinpoint where the flow has stopped. For most standard blockages, a set of drain rods is the first tool of choice: these are fed into the drain and used to physically break up and push through the obstruction. If that doesn't clear it, or if the blockage is further along the run, the engineer will move to high-pressure water jetting. This forces a concentrated stream of water through the pipe at high pressure, cutting through grease, scale, and compacted debris and flushing the whole run clean. For more complex cases — particularly relevant in the older stone-built properties and period cottages of Borthwickroad where root intrusion or pipe collapse is suspected — a CCTV drain survey may be recommended. This involves feeding a small camera through the drain to see exactly what's happening inside. You'll get a clear picture of the problem and a recommendation for any follow-up work, whether that's a repair, reline, or just a periodic maintenance jet. Most standard blockages in Borthwickroad are resolved within an hour.
pricing: For a standard blocked drain in Borthwickroad, expect to pay in the region of £80 to £130 for a straightforward internal blockage — a sink, bath, or toilet that needs rodding or a manual clear. External drain blockages or those requiring high-pressure jetting typically fall in the £120 to £180 range. If a CCTV survey is needed to diagnose a more complex issue, that can add £80 to £150 on top. Emergency or out-of-hours call-outs — which are common given that blockages rarely happen at convenient times — usually attract a surcharge, pushing the total towards the upper end of the £80 to £250 range. Older properties in Borthwickroad with more complex drainage layouts may also take longer to clear, which can affect the final cost.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickroad and the surrounding Midlothian area makes a genuine difference. Local engineers will be familiar with the age and style of drainage systems common to the older stone-built properties and period cottages here, and they'll have a realistic sense of what the ground conditions are like — important when dealing with displaced joints or root intrusion. Response times are quicker when someone is already working locally, which matters enormously when you've got a drain backing up into your home. A local professional also understands what council drainage responsibilities cover and where your private drain liability begins, which saves you time and hassle if a shared drain is involved.

faqs.q: How quickly can someone get to me in Borthwickroad for an emergency blocked drain?
faqs.a: Most drainage engineers covering Borthwickroad aim to reach you within one to two hours for a genuine emergency. Response times can vary depending on the time of day and how busy the area is, but because Borthwickroad is a small community, local trades often prioritise nearby call-outs. It's always worth calling ahead rather than booking online if it's urgent.

faqs.q: My period cottage in Borthwickroad has recurring drain blockages — what's likely causing it?
faqs.a: Recurring blockages in older properties are usually down to one of three things: tree root ingress into ageing clay pipes, a partial collapse or displaced joint creating a low point where debris collects, or a gradual scale build-up narrowing the pipe. In Borthwickroad's moderately hard water conditions, that last one is more common than people realise. A CCTV survey is the most reliable way to get a definitive answer.

faqs.q: Is a blocked drain in Borthwickroad my responsibility or Scottish Water's?
faqs.a: Generally speaking, drains within the boundary of your property are your responsibility. Once the drain connects to the public sewer network, it becomes Scottish Water's responsibility. However, shared private drains between neighbouring properties can be more complicated. If you're unsure, a local drainage engineer can help identify whether the blockage is on your section or further along the system.

faqs.q: Will high-pressure jetting damage the old pipes in my Borthwickroad stone-built property?
faqs.a: When carried out by an experienced engineer, high-pressure jetting is safe for the vast majority of pipes, including older clay and cast iron systems. The pressure is adjusted based on the pipe type and condition. If there's any doubt about the structural integrity of the pipework — which can happen in very old Borthwickroad properties — a CCTV inspection beforehand is the sensible approach.
